title: Conversational Mirroring SDK + Tool Safety — PRD sketch
body:
Summary:
This sketch proposes a "conversational mirroring" feature for the Hosted API SDKs: a lightweight streaming protocol that emits a canonical, verifiable mirror of the model's conversation state alongside incremental partial outputs and tool-call events. The goal is to improve client-side reconciliation, enable safe tool invocation patterns, and provide deterministic replay for debugging and evals while preserving low latency for interactive flows.

Why this problem matters:
- Current streaming payloads mix text deltas and opaque tool calls; clients must infer or reconstruct call boundaries which complicates SDKs (mobile/embedded) and leads to inconsistent retries and observable differences.
- Tool safety gates (e.g., policy checks, rate-limits) are harder to enforce when tool results are delivered as separate, unsynchronized messages.
- Product teams need a lightweight replay and verification signal for debugging regressions in structured output and tool chaining.

Target users and personas:
- Frontend engineers building conversational clients (web, mobile) who need deterministic render + tool wiring.
- Platform customers integrating third-party tools (search, DB writes) where auditability and safety matter.
- Internal QE and SRE for tracing regressions and analyzing tokenized cost breakdowns.

Goals (what success looks like):
- SDKs receive a synchronized "mirror stream" with typed frames: conversation_snapshot, text_delta, tool_call_start, tool_call_result, safety_annotation, checkpoint.
- Tool calls are emitted with signed IDs and canonical arguments; results include provenance metadata and optional safety verdicts.
- End-to-end latency for first byte remains within 1.1x of current streaming baseline on typical requests (p50).
- Developers can deterministically replay sessions using the mirror frames (server-provided replay token).
- Observability: trace token-level latencies and tool-call fallout (errors, safety blocks).

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not design the KMS/HSM signature system for privileged tool results — treat signatures as opaque string for now.
- Not a replacement for full trace logs or long-term archival; mirror streams are meant for live sessions and short-term replay (72h).

Design overview:
1) Mirror stream framing
- The server sends a typed streaming frame structure over the existing streaming channel (HTTP SSE / websocket / event-stream):
  - conversation_snapshot: periodic compact canonical state (timestamps, session id, turn ids, deterministic token hash)
  - text_delta: incremental generated text (same as current deltas but annotated with source turn id)
  - tool_call_start: emitted when the model requests an external tool (name, args_schema, call_id, predicted_cost_estimate)
  - tool_call_result: includes call_id, success/failure, result_payload (structured), signature_token, provenance_url (optional)
  - safety_annotation: policy signal for the chunk (block/soft-filter/high-risk reason codes)
  - checkpoint: durable snapshot with replay_token for deterministic replay

2) Structured output contract
- Tool call args and results must adhere to a JSON schema attached inline or by schema_id. SDKs will validate and surface errors.
- Results include minimal provenance: tool_version, region, latency_ms, and a signature token for later verification.

3) SDK ergonomics
- High-level client primitives: MirrorStream.session(), .on('delta'), .on('tool_call'), .on('tool_result'), .replay(token)
- Shadow mode: optional local-simulation hook where the SDK can simulate tool invocation locally and compare with returned result for telemetry without affecting production calls.
- Automatic idempotency: SDK auto-assigns call_ids and offers a retry policy for tool_call_start failures following server hints.
- Compact mobile mode: clients can subscribe to a reduced frame subset (text_delta + tool_call_start/result) to save bandwidth.

4) Safety and gating
- safety_annotation frames allow client UI to dim or hide content pending manual review.
- server-side policy engine may emit safety_annotation that triggers automatic tool-call cancellation (tool_call_result with status:canceled and reason). SDKs must surface this so integrators can avoid executing external actions.

Telemetry and metrics:
- Latency: first byte, time-to-tool-call-start, tool-call end-to-end latency, session replay success rate.
- Quality: mismatch rate between mirror snapshot and client-side reconstructed state, tool-result-provenance missing rate.
- Safety: percent of tool_call_start blocked by safety_annotation, distribution of reason codes.

Backward compatibility:
- Mirror frames are additive; older SDKs will ignore unknown frame types and continue to receive text deltas as before.
- Provide a feature-flag header so customers can opt into mirror streams per-API-key.

Operational plan / rollout:
- Alpha (4 weeks): internal SDKs + a few partner customers; non-default. Focus on stability of framing and signature token bootstrap.
- Beta (8 weeks): broader opt-in; add replay tooling in Console and lightweight replay UI for debugging.
- GA: after 12–16 weeks of beta and key metrics (latency increase <10%, replay success >98%).

Security and privacy considerations:
- Mirror frames may include tool args and partial content; default behavior is to mask PII in conversation_snapshot unless customer enables full fidelity.
- Signature tokens are short-lived; any signature verification happens client-side by calling a signature verification endpoint (rate-limited).

Risks and mitigations:
- Bandwidth increase: mitigate with compact mobile subscription and configurable snapshot cadence.
- SDK complexity: mitigate with high-level primitives and curated examples across JS, Python, Android, iOS.
- Safety false positives: provide manual override + audit logs for final decisions.

Open questions (needs engineering input):
- What is the exact shape of the signature_token? JWT-like or opaque id? (engineering)
- How large will conversation_snapshot be for long histories and how often should it be emitted to balance replay fidelity vs bandwidth? (product + infra)
- Should tool_call_result include a pointer to a server-hosted artifact (s3) for large results or inline only? (security/compliance)

Next steps and owners:
- Product: finalize frame schema and SDK primitive APIs (owner: Clara Nguyen) — 1 week
- Eng (serving-runtime): prototype frame emission and replay_token generation; validate p50 streaming latency (owner: Ravi Kapoor) — 2 sprints
- Eng (SDK): JS/Python minimal API and mobile compact mode (owner: Sofia Morales) — 3 sprints
- SRE: add telemetry for new metrics and run load tests (owner: Evan Li) — parallel

Appendix: example minimal stream (conceptual)
- conversation_snapshot {session_id: S, turn_id: 42, token_hash: H, replay_token: RT_123}
- text_delta {turn_id: 42, content: "Sure — I can look that up..."}
- tool_call_start {call_id: C1, tool: "search", args: {q: "redwood streaming sdk"}}
- tool_call_result {call_id: C1, status: "ok", result: {top_hit: "streaming-handshake"}, signature: "sig_v1_abc"}
- checkpoint {replay_token: RT_124}

Notes:
- This document intentionally focuses on the "mirroring" concept as a thin synchronization layer between the model's intent and the SDK's ability to render and safely act on outputs. It is complementary to existing streaming and structured-output work and aims to reduce client-side divergence and tool safety surprises.

Please review and add engineering estimates inline (linked JIRA tasks recommended).
